text:
maria: Heads up — saw weird client-side reorder when reconnecting to event-stream from the sample app. chunks arrived out of original order after a 502 and reconnect :confused:
aj: ugh. on which SDK? browser or node?
maria: browser (latest chrome). using the react-sampleapp with our browser-sdk v0.9.2.
aj: could be the resume-token handling. do you have a repro trace or logs?
maria: pasted console snippet:
```
EventStream onmessage #seq=42 data="{\"token\":\"abc\",\"chunk_index\":2}"
EventStream onmessage #seq=43 data="{\"token\":\"abc\",\"chunk_index\":1}"
```
so server seq increased but chunk_index dropped back.
dan: that looks like server sent fragments split across reconnection. resume token matched but we reassembled by seq not chunk_index.
ivy: hmm do we persist the last-processed chunk_index in local buffer or only last-event-id?
aj: currently client tracks lastEventId and replays fragments by their event-id order. we assume chunk_index monotonic within an event but apparently not if server re-shards streaming frames on reconnect.
ci-bot: deploy 2024-06-18T21:10 started for runtime v2.3 (note: streaming kernel changes).
maria: repro steps: 1) start sampleapp with small window; 2) trigger long response; 3) force 502 by flipping proxy in dev tools; 4) reconnect -> see reorder in UI.
aj: quick workaround — sort fragments by chunk_index before final assembly in the browser SDK. will that break other cases?
dan: sorting could mask true interleaving from multiplexed streams. better: include stream_id + chunk_index and drop duplicates/older indexes.
ivy: agreed. also add a check in debug mode to log if chunk_index decreases after resume.
maria: can we add a small fix in sampleapp first to reduce customer impact? sampleapp patch + SDK patch after.
aj: will open PRs: sampleapp patch to tolerate reorder, and SDK change to hold fragments in a map keyed by (stream_id, chunk_index) and apply strict duplicate suppression.
dan: please add an e2e test that simulates reconnection with shuffled delivery. add a CI job that runs the sampleapp-resume scenario.
aj: linking to draft PRs when created. tagging @ivy for review on safety of dropping lower-index duplicates.
ivy: happy to review. also document in devex notes that resumed eventstreams may deliver non-monotonic chunk indices — platform will aim to keep monotonic but clients should be defensive.
maria: thanks all. saving repro logs to the thread. :+1:
